EventKind.description: The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the domain that owns the event.
EventKind.title: EventKind

EventSource.description: Where an event came from, as the bare string the domain that raised it declares for itself.
EventSource.title: EventSource

ProviderPrint.description:
The provider's own identifier for the print an alert is about.

Held in the provider's representation — a 64-bit integer, which is what
every provider this system has met uses — and named for what it is rather
than for the provider, so that the supervision domain correlates on it
without knowing whose it is.

file_name.description: The file the provider named, when it named one.

id.description: The provider's own identifier for the print.

Timestamp.description: An instant in UTC, as an RFC 3339 string with a zero offset.
Timestamp.title: Timestamp

description:
One external body, read into an event under the adapter's own kind.

`kind` and `payload` are the [`EventBody`] flattened into this shape, so an
alert's wire form is the pair the store holds. `print` is what the
supervision domain correlates on; an alert about no print carries none.

image_url.description: The image this alert names, when it names one.

payload.description: What it carries, in the form its kind declares.

print.description:
The provider's own identifier for the print this alert is about, and
the file it named, when the alert is about a print at all.

title: NormalizedAlert
